_comment: Copy to ~/.config/starboard/config.json. Every key is optional — delete

Problems are reported in ~/Library/Logs/Starboard.log and never stop the
_comment_size: Width, x and height normally track the Dock and are not settable — that
is the point of the app. What you can change is how much fits in that
height: fontSize and padding together decide the row count. The defaults
give exactly two rows at a Dock height around 57-60pt.
Cmd+E (or the right-click menu) expands to full screen height; set
startExpanded to open that way. The fallback block below only applies
when the Dock cannot be read at all — no Accessibility permission, a
left/right Dock, or a Dock on a secondary display.
_comment_look: tint is Starboard's own layer over the system blur; alpha is the
transparency. Either { hex, alpha } or { red, green, blue, alpha } with
0...1 components. material is the NSVisualEffectView material behind it:
menu, popover, hudWindow, sidebar, titlebar, selection, headerView,
_comment_font: First name that resolves wins. Nerd Font variants come first because
prompt themes like Powerlevel10k draw separators from private-use ranges
_comment_palette: The 16 ANSI colours in order: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta,
cyan, white, then the bright variants. All 16 or none — a partial list is
reported and ignored rather than padded with colours you did not choose.
This only changes what an ANSI code renders as; which colour your prompt
theme picks for a segment is decided in your shell config.
